subject: Only one passage for a year: are dynamic occupancy models possible?

messages.author: b64bbb943d23ead1
messages.subject: Only one passage for a year: are dynamic occupancy models possible?
parts:
Hi everyone,
I inherited a dataset with 2 years of presence/absence data: 2 secondary occasions for the first year, and only one for the second year.
The best way to deal with it seemed to be dynamic occupancy modeling. Then I tried to pad a 4th column with NAs so as to create an artificial "4th passage". It actually works with colext, but goodness-of-fit tests give really bad results. I guess the problem is that it cannot model yearly estimates for the second year. Is there a way I could run dynamic occupancy models properly with this dataset?
It is about amphibian presence in ponds. Pooling the 3 passages could be a solution, but I cannot really meet the assumption of population closure...

Thanks a lot for your help!
Nadège

messages.author: 70621566ba652451
messages.subject: Re: Only one passage for a year: are dynamic occupancy models possible?
parts:
Seems to me like you're probably doing it right, but you just don't have enough data, which doesn't seem surprising given the situation you're describing. I imagine you could pull something like this off if you have enough sites surveyed, particularly in the first year, to make up for the limited number of years, although your strength of inference might still be limited with only two years depending on what you are trying to infer.

Also, you might be limited if your overall occupancy is really high or really low, in which case information for estimating persistence or colonization could be limited.

You could try data cloning to check if all your parameters are estimable, i.e., inflate your sample size by copying your data a bunch of times and variances for all your parameters of interest should approach zero. If they do, you at least know that the model is estimable and that sample size is probably what is limiting, although if sample size is limiting I'm not sure why you would get a poor result for goodness-of-fit. Usually, lack-of-fit indicates the model is missing or misrepresenting some source of variation.

messages.author: 247b990d236a7af6
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: Only one passage for a year: are dynamic occupancy models possible?
parts: The large negative estimates for colonization (-7.25 and -8.28) are due to there being no instances where the observed occupancy status goes from 0 to 1.  So the maximum likelihood estimate of the colonization probability is really 0 (with the logit of the colonization probability being minus infinity).  (And because of the stopping rules of the iterative process of the algorithm, it stops at the values you see.)

parts:
Sorry for my late answer; Thanks a lot for this explanation, you're absolutely right! There is only one site (out of 83) where the occupancy status goes from 0 to 1, for this species (but there are lots of 1 becoming 0).
So how can I use my models in that case, knowing the goodness-of-fit results are really bad?
I mean, this seems to be a reality: there are apparently no colonization events... (and I have a larger number of sites in year 2 than in year 1, so that I would really like to keep all my passages for power of explanation). Is that a limiting case or is there a solution?

Thanks again!
